title: Pasting of the orientation-free diagonal section comparison
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of [def-pur-conventions], with the specified global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the small pro-etale constructible exceptional inverse images and derived operations of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and let $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru^!Rv^!$ be the conjugate of compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\theta_{h,M}:Lh^*M\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!M$ be the specified tensor map [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps $u,v$ define
$$\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\circ\theta_{u,\omega_v}\circ\mathrm{sym}:\omega_u\otimes^LLu^*\omega_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{vu}.$$
For $h=f,g,gf$, write $W_h=\operatorname{dom}(h)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}\operatorname{dom}(h)$, $p_h$ for its first projection, $\Delta_h$ for the diagonal, $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant], and $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ for the specified diagonal base-change map [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change].

Put $Q=X\times_ZY$, $W=X\times_ZX$, $a:W\to Q$, $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1,f(x_2))$, $b:Q\to X$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, $t=\Delta_{gf}:X\to W$, and $s=(\operatorname{id}_X,f):X\to Q$. These formulas denote the maps induced by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $at=s$, $ba=p_{gf}$, and the Cartesian base-change maps identify $C_f\cong Lt^*\omega_a$ and $Lf^*C_g\cong Ls^*\omega_b$. Define the section-pasting comparison, using these maps and the monoidal pullback reassociation, by
$$\kappa:C_f\otimes^LLf^*C_g\xrightarrow{\sim}Lt^*(\omega_a\otimes^LLa^*\omega_b)\xrightarrow{Lt^*\sigma_{a,b}}C_{gf}.$$
Then
$$\alpha_{gf}\circ\kappa=\sigma_{f,g}\circ(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g).$$
The displayed comparisons commute with restriction to source and target open subschemes on which the morphisms restrict.

Here is the precise coordinate comparison. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B$, put $P_r=\mathbf A^r_B\to B$ [def-sbc-affine-space], let $z_r:B\to\mathbf A^r_B$ be its zero section, and put $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$. Let $q:\mathbf A^{d+e}_B=\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_B}\to\mathbf A^e_B$. Base change for the square defining $q$ identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*\omega_q$ with $D_d$, while pullback composition identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*\omega_{P_e}$ with $D_e$. Define
$$\nu_{d,e}:D_d\otimes^LD_e\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz_{d+e}^*(\omega_q\otimes^LLq^*\omega_{P_e})\xrightarrow{Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}}D_{d+e}.$$
On compatible etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] coordinate charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$ for $f,g$, with $U,V,T$ affine open subschemes of $X,Y,Z$, the coordinate differences in the second factors of the diagonal pairs identify $C_f|_U$, $Lf^*C_g|_U$, $C_{gf}|_U$ with $D_d,D_e,D_{d+e}$ over $B=U$. Under these comparisons, $\kappa|_U=\nu_{d,e}$. These are the canonical etale exceptional-pullback comparisons and monoidal pullback comparisons, and use no diagonal orientation or Tate-twist identification.

source.place: Proof Step 1: the remaining smooth-base-change and co-projection factors commute with the composite diagonal; canonical Cartesian product identifications

proof.text: Write $r:Q\to Y$ and $l:W\to X$ for the second projections. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the commutative diagram with rows $W\xrightarrow aQ\xrightarrow bX$ and $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, and vertical arrows $l,r,gf$. Its two squares are Cartesian: $W=Q\times_YX$ and $Q=X\times_ZY$. Its outer rectangle is the base-change square for $gf$, with $ba=p_{gf}$. Evaluation on pairs gives $at=s$, $lt=1_X$, and $rs=f$. Base-change and composition permanence [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence, lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] give the smooth separated finite-type maps $a,b,ba$ of dimensions $d,e,d+e$. These are the actual two squares used below; no square involving a composition isomorphism is regarded as a square of schemes.

Use $B_{h,v,N}:Lu^*Rh^!N\to Rh'^!Lv^*N$ for the transpose of $Lv^*\varepsilon_{h,N}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$ for a Cartesian square $(h,h',v,u)$; its unit specialization is exactly $\beta_{h,v}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. The horizontal law of [fix-lem-exchanges](2), inverted and followed by the pulled-back counit, gives transitivity of $B$ for successive base changes. The vertical law in the same clause, with compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition], gives
$$c_{b,a,L(gf)^*N}\circ B_{gf,gf,N}=Ra^!(B_{g,gf,N})\circ B_{f,r,Rg^!N}\circ Ll^*c_{g,f,N}.$$ This follows by taking the mates of the two sides of that vertical exchange equation, using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) and the composite counit [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; conjugation reverses composition as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Thus the geometric exchange equations, as well as the formal mate law, are used.

source.place: Step 1: smooth-base-change constituents; horizontal and vertical exchange pasting

proof.text:
The tensor and base-change clauses (1),(3) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] make every displayed $\theta$ and smooth $B$ invertible, and identify $B_{f,r,N}\,Ll^*\theta_{f,N}$ with $\theta_{a,Lr^*N}(1\otimes\beta_{f,r})$. Set
$$A=\beta_{f,r}:Ll^*\omega_f\to\omega_a,\quad B=\beta_{g,gf}:Lr^*\omega_g\to\omega_b,\quad D=\beta_{gf,gf}:Ll^*\omega_{gf}\to\omega_{ba}.$$
Apply the vertical identity of Step 2 at $N=\Lambda$, substitute this tensor compatibility at $N=\omega_g$, and invert $c_{b,a}$. Naturality of $\theta_a$ in $B$ gives exactly
$$D\,Ll^*\sigma_{f,g}=\sigma_{a,b}(A\otimes La^*B).\tag{*}$$
All pullback composition in this formula is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies its tensor comparison. Their reassociations agree termwise on K-flat flat-term models: both orders send a pure tensor to the same pulled-back tensor, and both composite pullbacks are the termwise canonical module comparison. This also fixes all suppressed associators.

source.place: Step 1: compatibility of smooth base change with the specified tensor-composition map

proof.text:
Let $i:W_f\to W$ send $(x,x')$ with $f(x)=f(x')$ to the same pair. Then $(W_f\xrightarrow iW, X\xrightarrow sQ)$ is the base-change square of $a$, and $i\Delta_f=t$. Let $j:Q\to W_g$ send $(x,y)$ to $(f(x),y)$; then $(Q\xrightarrow jW_g,X\xrightarrow fY)$ is the base-change square of $p_g$, and $js=\Delta_gf$. Put $F=\beta_{a,s}:Li^*\omega_a\to\omega_{p_f}$ and $G=\beta_{p_g,f}:Lj^*\omega_{p_g}\to\omega_b$. The comparisons in the statement are
$$\gamma_f=L\Delta_f^*F^{-1}:C_f\to Lt^*\omega_a,\qquad\gamma_g=Ls^*G:Lf^*C_g\to Ls^*\omega_b.$$
Horizontal transitivity from Step 2, applied respectively to the squares for $(f,r)$ then $(a,s)$ and for $(g,g)$ then $(p_g,f)$, gives
$$\alpha_f=(Lt^*A)^{-1}\gamma_f,\quad Lf^*\alpha_g=(Ls^*B)^{-1}\gamma_g,\quad\alpha_{gf}=(Lt^*D)^{-1}.$$
The last formula is precisely [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] for $gf$ since $lt=1$. The same lemma identifies the first two with the specified $\alpha$, rather than unspecified isomorphisms. Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] throughout to identify the composed pullbacks.

source.place: Step 1: diagonal section identifications and the actual base-change squares

proof.text:
The invertibility in [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] and adjunction conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of [thm-sf-comp-composition] show that each $\sigma$ is an isomorphism. The tensor pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $at=s$, and derived pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] make $\kappa$ exactly $Lt^*\sigma_{a,b}\circ(\gamma_f\otimes\gamma_g)$. Pull (*) back along $t$, precompose with $\gamma_f\otimes\gamma_g$, and multiply by $(Lt^*D)^{-1}$. The three substitutions of Step 4 give
$$\alpha_{gf}\kappa=\sigma_{f,g}(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g).$$
This is a calculation with the specified maps, requiring both exchange pasting and base-change compatibility of the tensor map.

source.place: Step 1: equality of the orientation-free diagonal-section comparison

proof.text:
We will also use the cocycle equation
$$\sigma_{vu,w}(\sigma_{u,v}\otimes1)=\sigma_{u,wv}(1\otimes Lu^*\sigma_{v,w}).\tag{**}$$
This is the tensor-formula composition clause (4) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] evaluated at $\omega_w$, followed by the inverse exceptional composition comparison: substitute $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$ on both sides. Naturality moves $c_{w,v}^{-1}$ through $\theta_u$; clause (4) replaces $\theta_u\circ Lu^*\theta_v$ with the composite tensor map; the two remaining $c$ composites agree because [thm-sf-comp-composition] is associative and conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] reverses the same associative equation. Thus (**) uses the specified $\theta$, not the unspecified isomorphism of the co-smooth-composition lemma. For an etale $u$, [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization](1),(3) say $\sigma_{u,v}^{-1}=E_{u,v}$ after removing $\omega_u$ with $\eta_u$. In particular (**) gives
$$E_{u,wv}\sigma_{vu,w}=Lu^*\sigma_{v,w}(E_{u,v}\otimes1).\tag{***}$$

source.place: Step 1: tensor reassociation, exceptional composition pentagon, and etale normalization

proof.text: Target-open restrictions are Cartesian base changes, so Steps 2-3 and [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2) identify every restricted $\beta$ and $\sigma$ with the corresponding map on the target open. A further source-open immersion $u$ uses the normalized etale comparison $E_{u,h}$ of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], rather than a falsely asserted Cartesian square. Its compatibility with $\sigma$ is (***); its compatibility with the Cartesian base-change maps is Step 2 with the etale normalization of that lemma. Restricting the diagonal pair amounts to restricting both factors, and its diagonal factors through that restriction. Hence applying the derived pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the formulas for $\gamma_f,\gamma_g,\kappa$ proves precisely their asserted compatibility with arbitrary compatible source and target open restrictions.

source.place: Step 1: compatibility with source and target open restriction

proof.text: For the base $B$ of the statement, [def-sbc-affine-space] and [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] give the smooth tower $\mathbf A_B^{d+e}\xrightarrow q\mathbf A_B^e\xrightarrow{P_e}B$. The square with top $\mathbf A_B^{d+e}\to\mathbf A_B^d$ and bottom $P_e$ is Cartesian and $q$ is the pullback of $P_d$. Its $\beta$ gives $Lz_{d+e}^*\omega_q\cong Lz_d^*\omega_{P_d}=D_d$, while $qz_{d+e}=z_e$ gives $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*\omega_{P_e}=D_e$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Thus the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and $Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}$ give the stated $\nu_{d,e}$. Its definition uses no trivialization of any dualizing object.

By Step 7 work on the stated charts and replace $(X,Y,Z)$ by $(U,V,T)$, putting $B=U$. Write $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ for the chart coordinates of $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ and $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_e)$ for those of $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$. With $Q=U\times_TV$ and $W=U\times_TU$, define
$$G:Q\to\mathbf A_B^e,\quad(u,v)\mapsto y(v)-y(fu).$$
Put $R=Q\times_{\mathbf A_B^e}\mathbf A_B^{d+e}=\mathbf A_Q^d$ with projections $q_Q:R\to Q$, $J:R\to\mathbf A_B^{d+e}$. Define
$$H:W\to R,\quad(u,u')\mapsto((u,fu'),x(u')-x(u)).$$
Then $a=q_QH$, $b=P_eG$, $qJ=Gq_Q$, and $F=JH$ has the ordered difference coordinates $(x(u')-x(u),y(fu')-y(fu))$. These formulas follow from [def-pc-fibre-product, def-sbc-affine-space]. $G$ is the base change of the chart of $g$, followed by translation by $-y(fu)$; $H$ is the base change of the chart of $f$, followed by translation by $-x(u)$. They are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]; translation is an isomorphism with inverse addition of the same coordinates. Likewise $J$ is etale as a base change of $G$. All these schemes are affine, so that cited affine ring-base-change statement applies, and all maps are separated finite type. Crucially the square $(W\xrightarrow F\mathbf A_B^{d+e},Q\xrightarrow G\mathbf A_B^e)$ need not be Cartesian; the square defining $R$ is Cartesian. The sections satisfy $Gs=z_e$ and $Ft=z_{d+e}$.

source.place: Step 1: compatible etale charts; factor the difference maps through a genuine Cartesian square

proof.text:
Write $E$ for the normalized comparisons of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. For the Cartesian square defining $R$, its clause (3) gives
$$E_{J,q}\sigma_{q_Q,G}=\beta_{q,G}^{-1},\tag{a}$$
after identifying $\omega_G$ with the unit. Apply (**) to $(q_Q,G,P_e)$ and (***) to $(J,q,P_e)$. Substitute (a) and $\sigma_{G,P_e}^{-1}=E_{G,P_e}$. Cancellation of the invertible $\sigma_{q_Q,G}$ gives the typed identity
$$E_{J,P_eq}\sigma_{q_Q,b}=LJ^*\sigma_{q,P_e}\bigl(\beta_{q,G}^{-1}\otimes Lq_Q^*E_{G,P_e}\bigr).\tag{b}$$
Both sides have domain $\omega_{q_Q}\otimes Lq_Q^*\omega_b$ and target $LJ^*\omega_{P_eq}$. Now apply (***) with $(H,q_Q,b)$, then pull (b) along $H$. Associativity of $c$ and the etale-composition normalization in that lemma identify $E_{F,P_eq}=LH^*E_{J,P_eq}\circ E_{H,bq_Q}$. Hence
$$E_{F,P_eq}\sigma_{a,b}=LF^*\sigma_{q,P_e}\bigl((LH^*\beta_{q,G}^{-1})E_{H,q_Q}\otimes La^*E_{G,P_e}\bigr).\tag{c}$$
This proves the comparison of the two towers using the Cartesian square and normalized etale factors separately.

source.place: Step 1: the affine chart tower comparison via the cocycle and the etale base-change normalization

proof.text: Check the input identifications in (c) against those defining $\kappa$. Pull the Cartesian square $(p_f,a,s,i)$ of Step 4 back through $H$. The result is the Cartesian square of etale maps $H:W\to\mathbf A_Q^d$ and $H_f:W_f\to\mathbf A_B^d$, with base $s:B\to Q$; explicitly $H_f(u,u')=(u,x(u')-x(u))$. Its zero section is the image of $\Delta_f$. The base-change compatibility of $\rho$ and $\eta$ in [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], and vertical exchange pasting [fix-lem-exchanges](2) for $a=q_QH$, identify $L\Delta_f^*E_{H_f,P_d}$ with $Lt^*E_{H,q_Q}\gamma_f$, followed by the base-change comparison for $q_Q$ along $s$. Horizontal exchange pasting identifies that comparison with $Lt^*LH^*\beta_{q,G}^{-1}$ followed by the $D_d$ comparison in Step 8: both are the inverse base-change comparison for $P_d$ along the composite $B\xrightarrow sQ\xrightarrow G\mathbf A_B^e$, with $Gs=z_e$. Thus the first input of $Lt^*$(c) is the actual difference-coordinate identification $C_f\to D_d$, using the route through $\gamma_f$, not an arbitrary isomorphism. For the second input define $G_g:W_g=V\times_TV\to\mathbf A_V^e$ by $(v,v')\mapsto(v,y(v')-y(v))$. The square with top $j:Q\to W_g$ and bottom $f:B\to V$ is Cartesian, as is the square of $G_g$ and $G:Q\to\mathbf A_B^e$ over the affine-space pullback $\mathbf A_B^e\to\mathbf A_V^e$. Vertical exchange pasting for $p_g=P_e^VG_g$, followed by etale beta normalization, identifies the pullback of the section comparison $L\Delta_g^*E_{G_g,P_e^V}$ with $Ls^*E_{G,P_e}\gamma_g:Lf^*C_g\to D_e$. All composed pullbacks here use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

source.place: Step 1: agreement of the chart comparisons with the section-invariant base-change route

proof.text: For the output, $Ft=z_{d+e}$ identifies $Lt^*E_{F,P_eq}:C_{gf}\to D_{d+e}$ with the canonical total difference-coordinate comparison; here $E_F$ is obtained by composing the etale comparisons for $H,J$, and [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization](2) makes this the canonical comparison for their composite. Pull (c) back along $t$ and insert $\gamma_f\otimes\gamma_g$. Step 11 identifies its two inputs with $D_d\otimes D_e$ exactly as in Step 8; its middle arrow is $Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}$. Its left side is the coordinate image of $\kappa$. This is precisely $\kappa|_U=\nu_{d,e}$. The tensor and pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] give all the displayed source/target identifications. The statement is conditional on compatible charts; their local availability follows by applying [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] first to $g$ and then to $f$. Empty charts cause no assertion; when either block has length zero the translation, zero section and cocycle calculations have the same formulas with the empty block, including the normalized etale unit. No orientation or Tate-twist comparison has entered.
